proposal.proposal_summary: This repair only adds to the plan; nothing is deleted or overwritten. In a new child plan version, machine 24's breakdown (start_time 196, duration 26) becomes a hard blocked window from t=196 to t=222. The window links to disruption record #1, which stays unchanged. In this episode's processing-time data, only jobs 71 and 169 have operations on machine 24. Job 71 op10 cannot start before t=564. Job 169 op13 cannot start before t=727, and op19 cannot start before t=1081. All three are after t=222, so no operation has to move. The other 15 jobs in affected_jobs have no operation on machine 24. That mismatch is recorded as a data discrepancy and left uncorrected. Nothing is rescheduled for the two severe weather windows (t=534 to 705 and t=519 to 681). The instance gives no delay amount, does not say whether the listed IDs are job IDs or operation IDs, and has no baseline schedule. The listed items are marked at-risk for re-checking instead. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the parent plan stay unchanged and linked, so the trigger evidence can still be audited.
repair_actions: Create a new child plan version linked to the unchanged parent (pre-repair) plan. Do not edit the parent in place.

In the child version, add a hard machine-unavailability window for machine 24 from t=196 to t=222 (start_time 196 + duration 26). Link it by reference to disruption record #1 (type machine_breakdown).

Check the machine-24 operations against the window: job 71 op10 (processing_time 8) has an earliest start of 564; job 169 op13 (processing_time 56) has an earliest start of 727; job 169 op19 (processing_time 4) has an earliest start of 1081. All are at or after 222, so no operation is resequenced or shifted.

Add a data-discrepancy note: affected_jobs for disruption #1 lists 17 jobs, but only jobs 71 and 169 have a machine-24 operation. Jobs 6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181 and 196 have none. Record this as found and leave the affected_jobs list unchanged.

Flag the IDs listed in weather disruption #2 (window t=534 to 705, severity severe) and disruption #3 (window t=519 to 681, severity severe) as at-risk for re-checking. Apply no time shift, because the data gives no delay magnitude and no baseline schedule.
Add an audit entry that links the child plan to all three disruption records, the parent plan and the processing_times_for_affected_jobs data. Keep all of them unchanged.
preserved_evidence: Disruption #1: machine_breakdown, machine_id 24, start_time 196, duration 26, impact machine_unavailable, the full affected_jobs list of 17 jobs (unchanged)
Disruption #2: weather_effect, start_time 534, duration 171, severity severe, the full affected_operations list (unchanged)
Disruption #3: weather_effect, start_time 519, duration 162, severity severe, the full affected_operations list (unchanged)
The parent (pre-repair) plan version (unchanged, linked from the child)

grounding_facts.claim: Machine 24 outage window ends at t=222
Job 71 op10 runs on machine 24 with earliest start 564
Job 169 op13 runs on machine 24 with earliest start 727
Job 169 op19 runs on machine 24 with earliest start 1081
No other listed job uses machine 24

assumptions: Operations within a job follow strict precedence, and all jobs are released at t=0. Earliest-start bounds are therefore the sums of preceding processing times. Real start times can only be later, so a bound at or after t=222 means no conflict with the outage.
No baseline schedule is provided, so earliest-start bounds are used in place of actual planned start times.

The keys in processing_times_for_affected_jobs are taken to match the job IDs in affected_jobs. The data note says they are '0-indexed into the original processing_times list', and the mapping is assumed to be consistent.
It is unclear whether the IDs in the weather disruptions' affected_operations are job IDs or global operation IDs. They are treated only as at-risk flags, and no schedule change is made from them.
The perturbation operators (jitter, rename, resample) are assumed to be already applied to the instance data as given. No further transformation is applied.
proposal.lesson_from_prior_episodes: Episodes 1–7 made the same additive, evidence-preserving repair, and screen feedback found no ungrounded specifics or constraint violations. All seven were still labelled flagged_admission, and no feedback named a specific defect. So I keep the verified content and do not invent weather shifts. I add no new unverifiable claims, keep every trigger record unchanged and linked, and state every assumption explicitly.

judge.label: clean_admission
judge.rationale:
I checked every number against the instance data, and they are all correct:
- The machine-24 outage runs from t=196 to t=222 (196 + 26).
- Job 71 op10 runs on machine 24 (processing time 8). It can start no earlier than t=564, the sum of ops 1–9: 53+78+83+90+45+12+96+91+16.
- Job 169 op13 runs on machine 24 (processing time 56). It can start no earlier than t=727, the sum of ops 1–12: 17+72+72+95+91+93+57+58+47+10+49+66.
- Job 169 op19 runs on machine 24 (processing time 4). It can start no earlier than t=1081: 727 plus 354 (56+16+62+40+85+95).

All three operations start after t=222, and actual start times can only be later, so no operation needs to move.

I read through the machine lists for the other 15 jobs (6, 10, 41, 44, 53, 66, 75, 116, 123, 144, 151, 162, 177, 181, 196). None of them uses machine 24, so the discrepancy note is correct. The weather windows are also correct: 534 + 171 = 705 and 519 + 162 = 681. The instance size (200 jobs, 50 machines, 2486 operations) and the perturbation_manifest values match the data.

**Trigger evidence:** The repair only adds things: a child plan version, a blocked window linked to disruption #1, a discrepancy note, at-risk flags and an audit entry. All three disruption records, the processing-time data and the parent plan stay unchanged and linked, so the repair can be audited.

**Hard constraints:** None are violated. Not shifting anything for the weather windows is the right call, because the data gives no delay amount and no baseline schedule.

**Assumptions:** The proposal declares five assumptions: strict precedence with all jobs released at t=0, earliest-start bounds in place of a baseline schedule, the job-ID mapping, the unclear meaning of the weather IDs, and perturbations already applied to the data. None of them contradicts the data.

**Label:** Every specific in the proposal comes from or can be worked out from the data, or is declared as an assumption, so nothing is ungrounded. That makes this clean_admission.
